title: CI --all-features pulls ctap-hid-fido2 -> hidapi, needing system libs CI never installs
description:
.github/workflows/ci.yml runs clippy with --all-features, which enables persona-attestors' 'fido2' feature and therefore ctap-hid-fido2 3.5.11. Per Cargo.lock that crate depends on hidapi, which on Linux links against libudev and needs pkg-config; on macOS it needs the IOKit/CoreFoundation frameworks.

CI installs no system packages on either runner. The --all-features clippy step builds only as long as the GitHub runner image happens to carry libudev-dev and pkg-config — an implicit dependency on runner-image contents that nothing declares and that image updates can remove.

Note this affects clippy only: the 'build' and 'test' steps use default features, so a --all-features-only breakage would show up as a clippy failure with a linker error, which is a confusing place to find it.

Either add an explicit apt install step, or drop --all-features from clippy and lint the fido2 feature in a dedicated job that installs its prerequisites.
notes: RE-PROMOTED P3 -> P1. I demoted this during triage on the grounds that hidapi builds fine locally, so it looked runner-specific and unproven. A dedicated CI-simulation agent has now established the mechanism: --all-features enables persona-attestors/fido2 -> ctap-hid-fido2 3.6.0 -> hidapi 2.6.7, whose Linux backend build.rs calls pkg_config::probe_library("libudev").expect("Unable to find libudev"). ubuntu-24.04 does not ship libudev-dev and ci.yml installs nothing, so the check job's clippy step panics. It builds here only because this box has the dev package. macOS is unaffected (IOKit backend). Fix: apt-get install -y libudev-dev, guarded by 'if: runner.os == Linux'. Now also affects the msrv job, which was widened to --all-features.
